meta.subject: math
meta.description: Fraction rules, decimal conversions, percent equivalents, ratios and proportions

facts.statement: A fraction represents a part of a whole, written as numerator over denominator (a/b)
The numerator is the top number showing how many parts are taken; the denominator is the bottom number showing total equal parts
A proper fraction has a numerator less than the denominator (e.g., 3/4), and its value is less than 1
An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to the denominator (e.g., 7/4), and its value is 1 or greater
A mixed number combines a whole number and a proper fraction (e.g., 1 3/4 = 7/4)
Equivalent fractions represent the same value: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8
To simplify a fraction, divide both numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor (GCF)
Any whole number can be written as a fraction with denominator 1: for example, 5 = 5/1
A unit fraction has a numerator of 1: examples are 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5
To convert a mixed number to an improper fraction: multiply whole number by denominator, add numerator, keep denominator. 2 3/5 = (2x5+3)/5 = 13/5
To convert an improper fraction to a mixed number: divide numerator by denominator. 17/5 = 3 remainder 2 = 3 2/5
To create equivalent fractions, multiply (or divide) both numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number
A fraction equals 1 when the numerator and denominator are the same nonzero number: 5/5 = 1
Comparing fractions with the same denominator: the fraction with the larger numerator is greater. 5/8 > 3/8
Comparing fractions with the same numerator: the fraction with the smaller denominator is greater. 1/3 > 1/5
Cross multiplication can compare fractions: a/b vs c/d, compare a*d to b*c. If a*d > b*c, then a/b > c/d
A fraction is in simplest form (lowest terms) when the GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1
The denominator of a fraction can never be zero because division by zero is undefined

common_errors.wrong: a fraction with a larger denominator is always larger
common_errors.correct: A larger denominator means smaller pieces. 1/8 is smaller than 1/4 even though 8 > 4.

common_errors.wrong: you can simplify by subtracting the same number from top and bottom
common_errors.correct: To simplify, divide both numerator and denominator by the same number, not subtract.

common_errors.wrong: 3/0 is a valid fraction equal to zero
common_errors.correct: A fraction with denominator 0 is undefined. Division by zero is not allowed.

common_errors.wrong: 0/5 is undefined
common_errors.correct: 0 divided by any nonzero number is 0. So 0/5 = 0 — it is a valid fraction.

common_errors.wrong: 2 3/5 as an improper fraction is 23/5
common_errors.correct: To convert, multiply whole number by denominator and add numerator: (2x5+3)/5 = 13/5, not 23/5.

common_errors.wrong: 3/4 is larger than 5/6 because 4 < 6
common_errors.correct: You must compare with common denominators: 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12. So 5/6 > 3/4.

facts.statement: To add or subtract fractions, they must have the same denominator (common denominator)
The least common denominator (LCD) is the smallest number that is a multiple of both denominators
To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators together and multiply the denominators together: (a/b) x (c/d) = (ac)/(bd)
To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: (a/b) / (c/d) = (a/b) x (d/c)
The reciprocal of a fraction a/b is b/a; the reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3
When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5
To add 1/3 + 1/4: find LCD = 12, convert to 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12
When multiplying mixed numbers, first convert to improper fractions: 1 1/2 x 2 1/3 = 3/2 x 7/3 = 21/6 = 3 1/2
Multiplying a fraction by its reciprocal always equals 1: (3/4) x (4/3) = 1
You can simplify (cancel) before multiplying fractions by dividing a numerator and a denominator by their common factor
To subtract fractions with unlike denominators: 3/4 - 1/3 = 9/12 - 4/12 = 5/12
When dividing whole number by a fraction: 6 / (1/2) = 6 x 2 = 12. Six halves make twelve halves (or 6 wholes worth of halves)
To add fractions with unlike denominators: 2/3 + 1/6 = 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6 (LCD is 6)
When adding three or more fractions, find the LCD of all denominators: 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1
Multiplying a number by a fraction between 0 and 1 makes it smaller: 12 x 3/4 = 9

common_errors.wrong: to add fractions, add both numerators and denominators: 1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7
common_errors.correct: You must find a common denominator first. 1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12.

common_errors.wrong: to divide fractions, just divide across: (2/3)/(4/5) = (2/4)/(3/5)
common_errors.correct: To divide fractions, multiply by the reciprocal: (2/3) / (4/5) = (2/3) x (5/4) = 10/12 = 5/6.

common_errors.wrong: multiplying fractions always gives a bigger number
common_errors.correct: Multiplying a fraction by a proper fraction gives a smaller result: 1/2 x 1/3 = 1/6, which is less than either.

common_errors.wrong: to subtract fractions, subtract numerators and denominators: 3/4 - 1/3 = 2/1 = 2
common_errors.correct: Find common denominator first: 3/4 - 1/3 = 9/12 - 4/12 = 5/12.
Dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2: 6 / (1/2) = 6 x 2 = 12.

common_errors.wrong: you can cancel across an addition sign: in (2/4) + (3/4), cancel the 4s to get 2+3=5
common_errors.correct: Cancellation only works in multiplication. In addition, keep the common denominator: (2/4)+(3/4)=5/4.

facts.statement: Decimals extend the place value system to the right of the decimal point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths
0.1 equals one tenth (1/10), 0.01 equals one hundredth (1/100), 0.001 equals one thousandth (1/1000)
A terminating decimal has a finite number of digits after the decimal point (e.g., 0.25, 0.5)
A repeating decimal has one or more digits that repeat infinitely (e.g., 1/3 = 0.333...)
To compare decimals, align the decimal points and compare digit by digit from left to right
Moving the decimal point one place to the right multiplies by 10; one place to the left divides by 10
To add or subtract decimals, align the decimal points and add/subtract column by column
When multiplying decimals, multiply as whole numbers then count total decimal places in both factors: 0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06 (2 decimal places)
When dividing by a decimal, move the decimal point in the divisor to make it a whole number, and move the dividend's decimal the same number of places: 4.8 / 0.6 = 48 / 6 = 8
To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator: 3/8 = 3 divided by 8 = 0.375
To convert a terminating decimal to a fraction, use place value: 0.75 = 75/100 = 3/4
Every terminating decimal can be written as a fraction with a denominator that is a power of 10: 0.125 = 125/1000 = 1/8
To convert 0.6 repeating to a fraction: let x = 0.666..., 10x = 6.666..., 10x - x = 6, 9x = 6, x = 6/9 = 2/3
Rounding 3.456 to the nearest hundredth: look at thousandths digit (6 >= 5), round up to 3.46

common_errors.wrong: 0.5 is less than 0.25 because 5 < 25
common_errors.correct: 0.5 = 0.50, which is greater than 0.25. Compare place values, not the digits after the decimal.

common_errors.wrong: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 exactly in computers
common_errors.correct: Due to floating-point representation, computers may store 0.1 + 0.2 as 0.30000000000000004, a well-known computer science fact.

common_errors.wrong: adding a zero after a decimal changes its value
common_errors.correct: 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500. Trailing zeros after a decimal point do not change the value.
Count decimal places: 0.3 (1 place) x 0.2 (1 place) = 0.06 (2 places total).

common_errors.wrong: when adding 1.5 + 2.35, line up the last digits
common_errors.correct: Align decimal points: 1.50 + 2.35 = 3.85. Add trailing zeros to align.

common_errors.wrong: 0.9 repeating is less than 1
common_errors.correct: 0.999... (repeating) is exactly equal to 1. This can be proven algebraically.

facts.statement: Percent means per hundred. 50% means 50 out of 100, or 50/100 = 1/2 = 0.5
To convert a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100: 0.75 = 75%
To convert a percent to a decimal, divide by 100: 25% = 0.25
To convert a fraction to a percent, divide numerator by denominator and multiply by 100: 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%
100% represents the whole amount; 200% is double the amount; 50% is half
To find a percent of a number, convert the percent to a decimal and multiply: 20% of 50 = 0.20 x 50 = 10
Percent increase = (new - original) / original x 100. If price went from $50 to $60, increase = (10/50) x 100 = 20%
Percent decrease = (original - new) / original x 100. If price went from $80 to $60, decrease = (20/80) x 100 = 25%
Sales tax is added to the price: $50 item + 8% tax = $50 x 1.08 = $54
A discount reduces the price: 30% off $80 = $80 x 0.70 = $56
To find what percent one number is of another: (part/whole) x 100. 15 is what % of 60? (15/60)x100 = 25%
Simple interest formula: I = P x r x t, where P is principal, r is rate (as decimal), and t is time in years
To find the original price before a discount: if the sale price is $42 after 30% off, original = $42 / 0.70 = $60
Compound interest grows faster than simple interest because interest is earned on previously earned interest

common_errors.correct: 50% of 80 = 0.50 x 80 = 40. To find a percent, convert it to a decimal first.
1/3 = 33.333...% (repeating). It is approximately 33.3%, not exactly 33%.

common_errors.wrong: a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease returns to the original
common_errors.correct: A 20% increase on 100 gives 120. A 20% decrease on 120 gives 96, not 100. Percent changes are not symmetric.

common_errors.wrong: to find 15% tip, divide by 15
common_errors.correct: To find 15% tip, multiply by 0.15: $40 x 0.15 = $6 tip.

common_errors.wrong: two successive 50% discounts give 100% off (free)
common_errors.correct: First 50% off $100 = $50. Second 50% off $50 = $25. You pay $25, not $0.

common_errors.wrong: a percent can never be more than 100%
common_errors.correct: Percents over 100% are valid: 150% of 40 = 60. Sales can grow 200%, meaning they tripled.

common_errors.wrong: to find the original price before a 25% discount, add 25% to the sale price
common_errors.correct: If sale price is $75 after 25% off, the original is $75 / 0.75 = $100. Adding 25% of $75 gives $93.75, which is wrong.

common_errors.wrong: 10% of a number is found by moving the decimal two places left
common_errors.correct: 10% means dividing by 10, so move the decimal one place left. 10% of 250 = 25, not 2.5.

facts.statement: A ratio compares two quantities: the ratio of 3 to 5 can be written as 3:5, 3/5, or '3 to 5'
A proportion is an equation stating that two ratios are equal: 1/2 = 3/6
A unit rate is a ratio with a denominator of 1: if 6 apples cost $3, the unit rate is $0.50 per apple
Cross multiplication solves proportions: if a/b = c/d, then a x d = b x c
Speed is a rate: distance divided by time. Traveling 150 miles in 3 hours = 50 mph
Equivalent ratios are found by multiplying or dividing both parts by the same number: 2:3 = 4:6 = 6:9
A scale on a map means a ratio between the map distance and real distance: scale 1:100 means 1 cm on map = 100 cm in reality
In a proportional relationship, the ratio between the two quantities stays constant: y/x = k (constant of proportionality)
A proportion can be solved by finding the missing value: 2/5 = x/15, so x = (2 x 15) / 5 = 6
Part-to-whole ratios differ from part-to-part: in 3 red and 5 blue, part-to-part is 3:5, part-to-whole is 3:8 or 5:8

common_errors.wrong: the ratio 3:5 is the same as 5:3
common_errors.correct: Order matters in ratios. 3:5 means 3 for every 5, while 5:3 means 5 for every 3.

common_errors.wrong: a ratio of 3:5 means there are 3 items total
common_errors.correct: A ratio of 3:5 means 3 parts to 5 parts, totaling 8 parts. It describes relative amounts, not absolute quantities.

common_errors.wrong: to find unit price, multiply cost by quantity
common_errors.correct: Unit price = total cost / quantity. $6 for 3 items = $6/3 = $2 per item.

common_errors.wrong: doubling a recipe means adding 2 of everything
common_errors.correct: Doubling means multiplying everything by 2. If recipe calls for 1/2 cup, doubling gives 1 cup, not 2 1/2 cups.

common_errors.wrong: a ratio of 2:3 means 2 out of 3
common_errors.correct: 2:3 is a part-to-part ratio meaning 2 parts to 3 parts. The part-to-whole would be 2 out of 5 (or 3 out of 5).

common_errors.wrong: to scale a ratio up, add the same number to both parts: 2:3 becomes 4:5
common_errors.correct: To create equivalent ratios, multiply both parts by the same number: 2:3 becomes 4:6 (multiply by 2), not 4:5.

facts.statement: To compare fractions with different denominators, find a common denominator and then compare the numerators
Benchmark fractions like 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and 1 help estimate and compare other fractions quickly
On a number line, fractions increase in value from left to right, just like whole numbers
Any fraction less than 1/2 has a numerator that is less than half its denominator: 3/8 < 1/2 because 3 < 4
When comparing fractions with the same numerator, the fraction with the smaller denominator is larger: 2/3 > 2/5 because thirds are bigger than fifths
To order fractions from least to greatest, convert all fractions to the same denominator, then order by numerator
Any positive fraction is greater than 0 and any fraction with numerator equal to denominator equals 1
Negative fractions are less than zero; -3/4 is less than -1/4 because -3/4 is farther left on the number line
To compare a fraction and a decimal, convert both to the same form: is 3/8 or 0.4 larger? 3/8 = 0.375, so 0.4 > 3/8
Between any two fractions, there are infinitely many other fractions: between 1/3 and 1/2, you can find 5/12, 2/5, 3/7, and more

common_errors.wrong: 3/5 > 4/7 because 5 < 7
common_errors.correct: You cannot compare by denominator alone. Convert: 3/5 = 21/35 and 4/7 = 20/35, so 3/5 > 4/7, but the reasoning must use common denominators.

common_errors.wrong: 1/3 = 1/4 because they are both one piece
common_errors.correct: 1/3 > 1/4 because dividing something into 3 equal parts gives bigger pieces than dividing into 4 equal parts.

common_errors.wrong: 2/6 > 1/3 because 2 > 1 and 6 > 3
common_errors.correct: 2/6 = 1/3 — they are equivalent fractions. You must simplify or find common denominators to compare.

common_errors.wrong: fractions are always less than 1
common_errors.correct: Improper fractions like 5/3 or 7/4 are greater than 1. A fraction is less than 1 only if the numerator is less than the denominator.

facts.statement: To add mixed numbers, add the whole number parts and fraction parts separately, then simplify: 2 1/4 + 3 1/4 = 5 2/4 = 5 1/2
When adding mixed numbers and the fraction sum exceeds 1, regroup: 2 3/4 + 1 3/4 = 3 6/4 = 3 + 1 2/4 = 4 1/2
To subtract mixed numbers when the fraction part of the subtrahend is larger, borrow 1 from the whole number: 5 1/4 - 2 3/4 requires regrouping 5 1/4 as 4 5/4
To multiply mixed numbers, convert each to an improper fraction first, then multiply: 1 1/2 x 2 2/3 = 3/2 x 8/3 = 24/6 = 4
To divide mixed numbers, convert each to an improper fraction and then multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor
3 1/2 as an improper fraction is 7/2 because (3 x 2 + 1) / 2 = 7/2
To convert 17/5 to a mixed number: 17 / 5 = 3 remainder 2, so 17/5 = 3 2/5

common_errors.wrong: to multiply mixed numbers, multiply the whole numbers and fractions separately: 1 1/2 x 2 1/3 = 2 1/6
common_errors.correct: You must convert to improper fractions first: 1 1/2 x 2 1/3 = 3/2 x 7/3 = 21/6 = 3 1/2, not 2 1/6.

common_errors.wrong: 5 1/4 - 2 3/4 = 3 2/4 because 5-2=3 and you just subtract fractions
2 3/5 as an improper fraction is 2 x 5 + 3 = 13, so it is 13/3
common_errors.correct: Keep the original denominator: 2 3/5 = (2 x 5 + 3)/5 = 13/5, not 13/3.

common_errors.wrong: to add mixed numbers, you can just add the whole parts and ignore the fractions
common_errors.correct: You must add both the whole number parts AND the fraction parts: 2 1/3 + 1 1/3 = 3 2/3, not 3.

common_errors.wrong: 3 1/2 / 1 1/4 = 3 because you just divide the whole numbers
common_errors.correct: Convert to improper fractions: 7/2 / 5/4 = 7/2 x 4/5 = 28/10 = 2 4/5, not 3.

facts.statement: When adding or subtracting decimals, always align the decimal points vertically before computing
When multiplying decimals, multiply as whole numbers, then place the decimal point so the product has the same total number of decimal places as both factors combined
1.5 x 2.3 = 3.45 because 15 x 23 = 345, and there are 2 total decimal places in the factors
To divide by a decimal, multiply both the divisor and dividend by a power of 10 to make the divisor a whole number: 3.6 / 0.4 = 36 / 4 = 9
Multiplying a decimal by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right; by 100, two places; by 1000, three places
Dividing a decimal by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the left; by 100, two places; by 1000, three places
When rounding decimals, look at the digit to the right of the rounding place: if it is 5 or more, round up; if less than 5, round down
Estimating with decimals: round each number to a convenient value first. To estimate 3.87 x 4.12, round to 4 x 4 = 16
Multiplying any number by 0.1 is the same as dividing it by 10: 45 x 0.1 = 4.5
Dividing a number by 0.5 is the same as multiplying it by 2: 7 / 0.5 = 14

common_errors.correct: Count total decimal places in factors (1 + 1 = 2). 15 x 23 = 345, place decimal to get 3.45, not 34.5.

common_errors.wrong: when dividing 4.8 / 0.6, just ignore the decimals and do 48/6
common_errors.correct: The method works (4.8/0.6 = 48/6 = 8), but you must move both decimal points the same number of places, not just ignore them.

common_errors.wrong: 2.5 + 3.15 = 5.40 because you line up the last digits
common_errors.correct: Align decimal points: 2.50 + 3.15 = 5.65. Do not line up the rightmost digits.

common_errors.wrong: 4.7 rounded to the nearest whole number is 4
common_errors.correct: 4.7 rounds to 5 because the tenths digit (7) is 5 or greater.

facts.statement: The three equivalent forms — fraction, decimal, percent — all represent the same value: 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%
To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator: 5/8 = 0.625
To convert a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 and add a percent sign: 0.35 = 35%
To convert a percent to a fraction, write the percent over 100 and simplify: 60% = 60/100 = 3/5
To convert a repeating decimal like 0.333... to a fraction: let x = 0.333..., then 10x = 3.333..., subtract to get 9x = 3, so x = 3/9 = 1/3
A fraction in lowest terms produces a terminating decimal only if the denominator's only prime factors are 2 and/or 5
To convert a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move decimal two places left): 6.5% = 0.065
Fractions, decimals, and percents can all be placed on the same number line: 1/4, 0.25, and 25% occupy the same point
To convert a mixed number to a percent, first convert to an improper fraction, then to a decimal, then to a percent: 1 1/4 = 5/4 = 1.25 = 125%

common_errors.wrong: to convert 3/8 to a percent, just put 3/8 next to a percent sign: 3/8%
common_errors.correct: First divide: 3/8 = 0.375, then multiply by 100: 0.375 x 100 = 37.5%.

common_errors.wrong: 0.25% is the same as 1/4
to convert 0.6 to a fraction, write 6/10 and that is the final answer
common_errors.correct: 6/10 is correct but should be simplified: 6/10 = 3/5.

common_errors.wrong: 1/3 = 0.33 exactly
common_errors.correct: 1/3 = 0.333... (repeating). 0.33 = 33/100, which is slightly less than 1/3.
